samples.summary: `TEMPLATE_BRIEFS` / `getTemplateBrief` have no consumer anywhere in the repo except their own spec — a whole new data layer (5 files, ~300 lines of content) that nothing reads.
samples.evidence: Grep for `TEMPLATE_BRIEFS|getTemplateBrief|TemplateBrief` matches only brief.ts, briefs*.ts and briefs.spec.ts. No route, service, CLI command or agent reads them, and the "fill agent" the docs describe does not exist in the tree. Speculative scaffolding that will rot against the templates it mirrors (slug/field drift is only checked for slug existence).

samples.summary: `themedDeck` re-implements `slide()` and `deck()` rather than reusing them: layout lookup, `applyLayoutToSlide`, the placeholder-fill loop and the document envelope are duplicated verbatim, so the two authoring paths can now diverge.
samples.evidence: builders.ts:101-148 (`slide`, `deck`) and the new :357-… body of `themedDeck` contain the same 'find layout or throw', the same `applyLayoutToSlide` call, the same `placeholders.forEach` re-keying with `${target.id}-p${li}`, and the same `{ meta, themes, masters, layouts, slides } as SlidesDocument` return. `themedDeck` could have been `deckOn(theme, title, specs.map(([id, texts]) => slide(id, texts, theme)))` with one extra parameter on `slide()`.

samples.summary: The `Decor` shape painter hand-rolls slides model types (`Fill`, an untyped `shapeEl(): unknown`, `as unknown as typeof slide.elements`, and an `inl.style` cast through `Record<string, unknown>`), defeating the stated reason the catalogue is TypeScript at all.
samples.evidence: template-gallery.md:1008-1011: the catalogue "lives in packages/backend/src/template/seed/catalog/ as TypeScript rather than JSON or binaries, so it typechecks against the real document models". The new code declares its own local `Fill` union and returns `unknown` from `shapeEl`, then casts the array into `slide.elements`, so none of the emitted shape elements are checked against the slides package's `ShapeElement`/fill types — a composition preset that is structurally wrong reaches the seeded gallery unchecked. Slide composition is also arguably slides-package territory (it owns layouts, themes and element shapes) rather than a backend seed helper.

samples.summary: `const SW = 1920; const SH = 1080;` re-declare the slide canvas constants instead of importing `SLIDE_WIDTH` / `SLIDE_HEIGHT`, which the change's own package entry already exports.
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/node.ts:46-47 exports `SLIDE_HEIGHT` and `SLIDE_WIDTH` (defined at packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:269). builders.ts already imports from `@wafflebase/slides`, so the literals are an avoidable second source of truth for the canvas size.

samples.evidence: SKILL.md:9-10 — "Frontmatter: Every skill has YAML frontmatter with `name`, `description`, `safety`, and `tools` fields" — and SKILL.md:36-43 lists the four Slides skills in a table that slides-author.md is absent from. slides-manage.md:1-11 shows the required frontmatter block. verdict.reason: Every quoted location checks out. brief.ts:1-38 really does define a per-template slot schema (FieldType/FieldSpec/TemplateBrief) and documents itself as the values "a fill agent collects from the user before it fills the blank template's placeholders", with the seed catalogue shipping "<placeholder>" slots (confirmed in slides-more.ts:25,73,95,124,178,228). It is populated, not a stub: briefs.ts:33-56 aggregates 17 briefs plus a getTemplateBrief() lookup. docs/design/template-gallery.md:53 lists "parameterized slots" as a Non-Goal, :82-85 says CapCut-style replaceable slots are "declined, not deferred pending evidence", and :1091-1103 records the identical idea (placeholder convention collected at use time and substituted) as a decision NOT to build. Nothing in docs/design/ amends that decision — the doc's own seed section (:980-1020) describes the catalogue with no mention of blank templates, placeholders, briefs or a fill agent, and grep for brief/fill agent/TemplateBrief across docs/design/ yields no relevant hit. So this is scope past a stated Non-Goal with no design-doc amendment, which this lens grades major/blocking. The only mitigating fact I found (no runtime consumer; only briefs.spec.ts imports it) is a severity nuance, not a refutation ground.
